O.outcome_detail: A-level integrative and instrumental foreign-language motivation

result.effect: integrative motivation d=.95; instrumental motivation d=.50

cells.quote: When Table 3 is examined, it can be seen that there is a significant difference in integrative and instrumental motivation levels of treatment and control groups at p < 0.05 level (p = .00 < .05; p = .02 < .05 ). This means that the integrative and instrumental motivation is significant in favor of the treatment group.
cells.note: The study does not state that students were randomly assigned; A-level analyses used change scores because ANCOVA assumptions were not met.

O.outcome_detail: B-level integrative and instrumental foreign-language motivation

result.effect: integrative motivation d=.54; instrumental motivation effect size not printed

cells.quote: When Table 5 is examined, it can be seen that there is a significant difference in integrative motivation levels of treatment and control groups at p < 0.05 level (p = .00 < .05). This means that the integrative motivation is significant in favor of the treatment group.
cells.note: For instrumental motivation, the reported ANCOVA also found a significant treatment-group advantage after controlling pre-test scores (F=5.40, p=.02), but no effect size was printed.

O.outcome_detail: instrumental motivation post-test

O.outcome_detail: A-level students’ integrative foreign-language motivation gain

cells.quote: When Table 3 is examined, it can be seen that there is a significant difference in integrative and instrumental motivation levels of treatment and control groups at p < 0.05 level (p = .00 < .05; p = .02 < .05 ). This means that the integrative and instrumental motivation is significant in favor of the treatment group. On the other hand, when d value, which was calculated via Cohen’s d formula, is examined, it is seen that the effect size of in tegrative motivation is .95.
